positioning: The African lion hound with a ridge of its own.
story: Look at the back of a Rhodesian Ridgeback. A strip of hair grows the wrong way, from the tail toward the shoulders. It is the ridge, and it defines the breed.
The story begins in southern Africa. European settlers brought hounds and guard dogs. They bred them with the half-wild, ridged dogs of the Khoikhoi people.

Hunters in Rhodesia used the dogs to track lions and hold them at bay until the hunter arrived. People called the breed the African Lion Hound. The dogs did not fight the lion. They kept it busy and kept clear.
In 1922, breeders in Bulawayo wrote the first standard. The AKC recognized the breed in 1955.
At home, a Ridgeback is calm indoors and a rocket outdoors. It is dignified, loyal, and sometimes stubborn. It bonds with its family, and it keeps its opinion of strangers private.
Give it miles to run and a firm, kind leader. It will give you a lifetime of quiet company.
rank_cap: Africa’s lion hound, ridge and all (AKC)
fblocks: Rhodesian for the African region where the breed was standardized. Ridgeback for the stripe of hair along its spine.
Few are famous by name. The breed is the legend, bred to hold lions at bay across the African bush.
Strong, smart, and independent. Needs steady training and daily running. Ask breeders about dermoid sinus, a skin defect.
A short, sleek coat in light to red wheaten. The ridge forms two matching crowns. A dark mask is common.
Seventy to eighty-five pounds. Standard written in 1922. Recognized by the AKC in 1955.
days: Old Jabari rests in the rock shade. The desert can do its worst. He is not moving.
The ridge grows backward along the spine. Every Ridgeback has one.
Ridgebacks held lions at bay in Africa. A thunderhead is nothing.
Two Ridgebacks climb the canyon trail. The cliffs are not impressed.
A horned lizard holds still. So does Zuri. Respect looks like patience.
A show ridge needs two matching whorls, called crowns. Dust is optional.
Puppies sleep against old Jabari by lantern light. He has seen many deserts.
last_walk:
The sky goes plum, and the saguaros stand like sentries.
Kofi and Zuri walk the dusty road home. Their coats match the dust, and their ridges catch the last light. A Ridgeback is a lion hound by trade and a house cat by evening. The lantern is lit at camp.
